title: fix(rootless): preserve systemd socket activation fds on re-exec
body:
When podman.service is socket-activated at user login it races with the other podman units to set up the rootless pause process.  If the re-executed child loses the race for the pause PID file, podman falls back to reexec_userns_join(), which forks again.

see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29964

>  I think we should still close these fds when the race succeeds, can you use this diff instead?

But why? I mean what do we gain by closing the fds in the parent exactly? I really do not follow the logic of unsetting the env and closing the fds in the parent process. They could just stay open there as they are not used. The process exits directly after the child so it is not like it would hold them open for much longer?
